universities.name: \. Chalmers University of Technology
universities.desc: Chalmers offers an English-taught **MSc in Electrical and Electronics Engineering**. This is a two-year programme with specialization opportunities in Integrated Circuit Design, Semiconductor Devices and Technology, Systems and Signals, and Microwave and Photonics. Students gain knowledge of advanced electronic systems and semiconductor-related research. **![][image1]**

universities.name: \. KTH Royal Institute of Technology
universities.location: \. KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden
universities.desc: KTH offers an English-taught **Master's in Embedded Systems** with an Embedded Electronics track. It covers subjects such as circuit boards, application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and system-on-chip design. This programme is an alternative for students interested in electronic hardware and embedded technology. **![][image2]** These institutions are among the **Best Universities for Electronics Engineering in Sweden** to explore for postgraduate education. Students should confirm the exact programme title, curriculum, tuition fees and eligibility criteria directly with each university.

items.q: Can Indian students apply for Electronics & Communication (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, Indian students with qualifying credentials meeting English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) and academic prerequisites can apply to recognized universities in Sweden.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction for Electronics & Communication (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Most master's and international bachelor's degree programmes are taught entirely in English for international students across Swedish universities.

items.q: What are the typical tuition fees for Electronics & Communication (PG) in Sweden?
items.a: Tuition fees for international students generally range between SEK 80,000 and SEK 150,000 per year, depending on the institution and level of study.

items.q: Can international students work while studying in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, non-EU international students holding a valid Swedish residence permit for higher education are permitted to work alongside their studies without a fixed hours limitation during term time.
